newsitem.title: USA: U.S. child sues over snacktime Cabbage Patch doll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. child sues over snacktime Cabbage Patch doll.

text.p: A Los Angeles attorney filed a lawsuit on Friday seeking $25 million in punitive damages on behalf of a nine-year-old girl whose hair was allegedly chewed up by a "Cabbage Patch Doll".
Attorney George Najjar said the suit was filed against Mattel Inc, which makes the doll, and Wal-Mart Stores Inc where the toy can be bought.
Najjar said his client, Jessica Wells, awoke screaming Dec. 29 to find the Cabbage Patch Snacktime Kids Doll had consumed her hair to her scalp.
The battery-operated doll is designed to chew and consume plastic food.
The suit was filed in San Diego County Court on behalf of Jessica and her parents, Tom and Genie Taylor. Mattel had no immediate comment on the lawsuit and Wal-Mart could not be reached for comment.
Mattel recently announced plans to refund $40 to owners of the dolls and discontinue production of them. The decision comes following more than 35 complaints of chewing incidents.

"When companies choose profits over safety, they should be punished accordingly," said Najjar. "Only signficant monetary penalties will deter major corporations from testing products on our children," he said.
